open.speaker: lk_yellowcoat
lines: lk_yellowcoat
Hiya! Kerry. Kids' club, the donkey derby, and the glamorous granny on Fridays, which is a job and a half. You're not with a coach. Are you the Americans?
lk_yellowcoat
Terry said don't talk to the Americans, so obviously. Have a lolly, they're free, they're for the kids, you look like you need one.
lk_yellowcoat
Don't tell Terry about the lolly.
dale
Twenty-two, three weeks into the season, and she's already got a list of things not to tell Terry. Good.

passives.line: The smile is real and she has been using it on frightened children all week. There is something under it she's been smiling at too.
A kids' club cassette recorder hangs off her shoulder with a tape in it, wound back. She has been listening to something and rewinding it.

options.text: We'll take a lolly. How's the kids' club this week?
What else aren't we telling Terry?
The notice in the office. No walkabouts without the manager. Why?

kind.speaker: lk_yellowcoat
lines: lk_yellowcoat
Busy. Forty on the register, three sick, one bit a donkey. Normal. Mostly normal.
lk_yellowcoat
Three of them won't go on the field. Different coaches, different mums, and they all want to stay in the ballroom with the lights on. In May. That's not normal.

wry.speaker: lk_yellowcoat
lines: lk_yellowcoat
Loads. The fruit machine pays out if you hit it on the left. Gaz does Uncle Rainbow's voice better than Uncle Rainbow. There's a hat in the store we're not to touch.
lk_yellowcoat
...I've touched it. Don't tell Terry. That's going to be a long list with you lot, isn't it.

hard.speaker: lk_yellowcoat
lines: lk_yellowcoat
Oh, that one. Terry's one rule. Nobody knows why and nobody asks twice, because Gaz asked twice.
lk_yellowcoat
You're direct. That's fine. I do forty six-year-olds a day, I can do four of you.

hub.speaker: lk_yellowcoat
hub.prompt: Go on, ask. Kids' club's at two and I've got the donkeys till then.
lines: lk_yellowcoat
Go on, ask. Kids' club's at two and I've got the donkeys till then.

static.line: The tape. She's rewound it to the same place twice since you walked up. There's a voice on it that isn't a child's. Make her play it.

options.text: What's the kids' club singing this week? There's always a song.

fail.line: The Birdie Song, and if you make me do the actions I'll never speak to you again. Next question.

options.text: Gaz got barred for asking twice. What did he ask the second time?
Play us the tape, Kerry. The bit you keep rewinding to.
The hat band's got Brylcreem in it. Somebody wore it a whole season.
We'll let you get back to the donkeys.

song.speaker: lk_yellowcoat
lines: lk_yellowcoat
That's the thing. I didn't teach them one. Monday they were all singing it anyway, the three off the field and then the rest.
lk_yellowcoat
'Come and see the dials, come and see the dials.' To the tune of nothing.
lk_yellowcoat
I asked who taught them. They said the yellow man. I said Uncle Rainbow? They said no. The other one.
elijah
Children learn a song from whoever sings it to them. Somebody sang it to them.

gaz.speaker: lk_yellowcoat
lines: lk_yellowcoat
First time he asked why no walkabouts and Terry said because I said. Second time he'd found the rota in Len's office. He said, who's Sunny Jim, Terry, and what did he do?
lk_yellowcoat
Terry went the colour of the ballroom carpet and barred him for a week and bought him a drink the same night. Both. Gaz said it was like being told off by somebody drowning.
teddy
Barred and bought a drink. That's a man paying for silence and apologising for the price.

gaz_fail.speaker: lk_yellowcoat
lines: lk_yellowcoat
Dunno. Something about the bar. Gaz asks about the bar a lot.
lk_yellowcoat
Len would know. Len knows what everyone asked and when. He's in the office when Terry isn't and the other way round.

tape.speaker: lk_yellowcoat
lines: lk_yellowcoat
...Okay. Okay. It's the kids doing the song, Tuesday, I taped it to show Terry. Listen under them. Right there. Hear that?
lk_yellowcoat
That's not a kid. That's not Gaz. It's flat, like a kazoo, and it's doing the song a beat ahead of them. Like it's leading. There was nobody in the room. I'd have seen.
lk_yellowcoat
I've rewound it about fifty times. It's there every time. I thought if I played it enough it'd be a kid.
june
A beat ahead. It's not on the tape by accident. It's on the tape because it wanted to be.

tape_fail.speaker: lk_yellowcoat
lines: lk_yellowcoat
...It's chewed. It's chewed it. The machine's just eaten the... that's the only one. That was the only one.
lk_yellowcoat
Just go. Please. Go and ask Len, go and ask anybody, I've got donkeys.
vera
The machine didn't chew it. Something took it back.

lab.speaker: lk_yellowcoat
lines: lk_yellowcoat
Brylcreem. Right. Twenty-one years in a store and it's still greasy, I know, I've had it on my hands.
lk_yellowcoat
Here's the thing. It was greasy on Monday and it's greasier now. Like somebody's wearing it. And the store's padlocked and the padlock's new and I've not got the key.
ruth
Somebody is wearing it, love. Just not while you're looking.
